la:adj:madidus.html:
mădĭdus, a, um, adj.
madeo
,
moist, wet, soaked, drenched (rare until after the Aug. per.).
Lit.
In gen.: fasciculus epistolarum aquā madidus, * : spiritus,: madidi myrrhā capilli,: madidis Notus evolat alis,; cf. Cort.: genae,i. e. bedewed with tears,: comae,moistened with unguents,: fossae,wet, abounding in water,: palus,: lacus,: Juppiter,i. e. Pluvius,: ver,rainy,. —*
With gen.: rosas madidas divini roris et nectaris video,.—
In partic.
Dyed: vestis cocco madida, vel murice tincta,. —
Drunk, intoxicated: madidus vino,: faciam ut sit madidus sobrius,: cum peteret matellam madidus,; : illum madidum, nihili incontinentem, etc.,a drunkard, sot,: molli luxu madefacta meroque,: dies,i. e. spent in drinking,: Tarentum,full of drunkenness,. —
Transf., soft, boiled soft, sodden, soaked: madidiora lenticula,: madida quae mihi apposita in mensam,; : cicer,; : siliginis offas accipere et madidae,: tabe jecur madidum,putrid, corrupt,.—
Trop. *
Soft, weak: madida memoria, Caecil. ap. P. (Com. Rel. v. 31 Rib.).—
Full of, filled with any thing: Minervae artibus,: madidi jocis libelli,.— Hence, * adv.: mădĭdē, moistly: non vides me uti madide madeam?how thoroughly soaked, drunk, I am,.

la:verb:madefacio.html:
mădĕfăcĭo, fēci, factum, 3,
v. a.; in pass.: mădĕfīo, factus, fĭĕri
madeo, facio
, to make wet, to wet, moisten, to soak, drench, water, etc.
In gen.: lanam aceto et nitro,: amarantus madefactus aquā revirescit,, 8, 23, § 47: radix in vino madefacta,: spongiam (opp. exprimere),: ne libelli madefierent,: imbuti sanguine gladii, vel madefacti potius,; cf.: Graeciam madefactum iri sanguine,; : caules,to soak, steep,: terram suo madefecit odore,steeped,.—Poet.: caris vellera sucis bis madefacta,i. e. dyed,.—
In partic., to drench with wine, to intoxicate, make drunk (poet. and in post-class. prose): eo vos vostrosque adeo pantices madefacitis, quom ego sim hic siccus, * : multo madefactus Iaccho, Col. poët. 10, 309: poculis amplioribus madefacit,; cf.: molli luxu madefacta (membra),.
la:verb:madefacio.inflection: fēci, factum, 3, v. a., factus, fĭĕri

la:verb:madesco.html:
mădesco, dŭi, 3,
v. inch. n. [madeo], to become moist or wet (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: semiusta madescunt Robora,: tellus Nubibus assi

duis pluvioque madescit ab austro, : multā terra madescit aquā,: nec madescimus nisi umore, * : spectare oportet, num tempora paulum madescant, become moist, i. e. perspire, —Poet.: quibus invito maduerunt sanguine dextrae,have killed,; cf.: nati maduere paterno Sanguine,.—*

In partic., to get drunk, become intoxicated: quem (Chrysippum) cotidie ferunt madescere solitum, Mai.—
Transf., to become soft: ne umore madescant ungulae,; ; id. poët. 10, 398: triticum madescit dulci aquā ligneis vasis,.

senses: to be softened by boiling; to be sodden or boiled
to be full overflow with; to abound in
la:verb:madeo.html:
mădĕo, ŭi, ēre, v. n.
Gr. μαδάω, to drip; cf. Sanscr. mad-, to be merry; Gr. μαστός and μεστός
,
to be wet or moist, to drip or flow with any thing (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: natabant pavimenta vino, madebant parietes,: Persae unguento madent,: plurima fuso Sanguine terra madet,: vere madent udo terrae,: radix suco madet,: lacrimis madent genae,are moistened, bedewed,: cruore maduit,: nec umquam sanguine causidici maduerunt rostra pusilli,: metu, to sweat or melt with fear, .—
In partic.
To be drenched with wine, to be drunk, intoxicated: membra vino madent,: ecquid tibi videor madere?: madide madere,: festā luce madere,. —Poet.: tardescit lingua, madet mens, Nant oculi (of a drunken man),his senses fail,.—
To be softened by boiling, to be boiled, sodden (mostly in Plaut. and Verg.): jam ergo haec madebunt, faxo,: collyrae facite ut madeant et colyphia,: ut, quamvis igni exiguo, properata maderent,: comedam, inquit, flebile nati sinciput Pharioque madentis aceto,; cf.: commadeo, madesco.—
Transf., to be full of, to overflow with, to abound in any thing (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): madeant generoso pocula Baccho,be filled up to the brim,: madent fercula deliciis,Caecubae vites in Pomptinis paludibus madent,: arte madent simulacra,: quamquam Socraticis madet Sermonibus,is full of, familiar with,; cf.: cujus Cecropia pectora voce madent,i. e. perfectly versed in the Greek language,. —Hence, mădens, entis, P. a.
Lit., wet, moist.
In gen.: madentes spongiae,: campi, wet, marshy (corresp. to paludes), : vestis madens sanguine,dripping,: nix sole madens,i. e. melting,: umor sudoris per collum,flowing,: crinis,flowing, abundant,: Auster,i. e. rainy,; so, bruma,: deus,i. e. Neptune,: Lamiarum caede,reeking with,.—
In partic., drunk, intoxicated: mersus vino et madens,; so absol.: distentus ac madens,; cf.: ille meri veteris per crura madentia torrens,.—
Transf., full, filled, imbued with something: jure madens, full of, i. e. skilled in law, : intercutibus ipsi vitiis madentes,full of,: cui felle nullo, melle multo mens madens,.
